summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that the Prophet was greatly concerned for all of mankind to accept Imaan, and Allaah revealed verses telling him that guidance and misguidance are decreed.
When Abu Taalib was dying, the Quraysh complained about the Prophet; Abu Taalib asked him to stop, and the Prophet asked only that they say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah.
Quraysh leaders ask Abu Taalib to mediate; the Prophet offers them one statement, Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and they refuse and leave.
notes: Abu Sufyaan here is the pre-Islaam Abu Sufyaan bin Harb, as in the approved entry.

summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyab reports that Abu Taalib died under pressure from Abu Jahal and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah, and that the Prophet was then told not to seek forgiveness for the Mushrikeen.
notes: The father who is the source of this report is not named in the text, so he is left out.

summary: Another report says Abu Taalib died without reciting the Kalimah while Abu Jahal and Abdullaah bin Abi Umayyah repeated their objections, and that the two verses were revealed afterwards.
notes: No narrator is named. The verses referred to are those quoted in n00004.

summary: Abu Hurayrah narrates that the Prophet asked Abu Taalib on his death-bed to say Laa Ilaaha Illallaah, and Abu Taalib refused for fear of Quraysh ridicule; the verse Qasas 56 was revealed on that occasion.
Aqeel bin Abi Taalib narrates that Abu Taalib asked the Prophet to stop saying things that hurt the Quraysh, and the Prophet refused, saying he could not stop what he was sent to do.

Abu Taalib asks the Prophet to stop, and the Prophet refuses even if the sun and moon were placed in his hands; Jaabir then narrates how Utba bin Rabee'ah failed to bargain the Prophet off and was moved by his recitation of Surah Sajdah.
notes: Two reports are joined: the Bayhaqi narration about Abu Taalib, then Jaabir's longer report about Utba. The Quraysh are unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar narrates that Utba bin Rabee'ah offered the Prophet wealth, position and leadership to stop his preaching; after the Prophet recited Surah Sajdah, Utba told the Quraysh to leave him alone.
notes: Utba is also called Abul Waleed in the text.

summary: Miswar and Marwaan report that Budayl bin Waraqa told the Prophet that the Quraysh were ready to fight, and the Prophet replied that he came only for Umrah and offered a treaty, vowing to fight if they refused Islaam.
notes: This is part of a lengthy report on Hudaybiyyah; the text opens with 'Part of the narration states', so it begins mid-report. Marwaan's sahabi status is unsure in the approved list.

summary: The Tabraani version, also from Miswar and Marwaan, has the Prophet declare that he will fight the Quraysh for the Deen until victory or his death if they refuse Islaam and still fight.
notes: A variant of the report in n00010. Tabraani is the collector cited and is not tagged.

summary: Sahal bin Sa'd narrates that at Khaybar the Prophet gave the flag to Ali, who was cured of eye pain by the Prophet's saliva, and that Ali was told to invite the people to Islaam before fighting.
Miqdaad bin Amr narrates that he took Hakam bin Kaysaan prisoner, Umar wanted him executed, and the Prophet kept inviting Hakam until he accepted Islaam.
notes: Miqdaad is the narrator and also acts in the story, so he is tagged subject.

summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates that Wahshi bin Harb, who killed Hamza, asked whether he could be forgiven; after a series of verses that answered each objection, he accepted Islaam.

Ibn Abbaas narrates verses revealed for murderers and adulterers who asked about expiation; a second report from Abu Tha'laba Khushani describes Faatima weeping at the Prophet's pale, tired appearance after a journey.
notes: Two reports are joined; the second is headed 'Hadhrat Faatima Weeps at the Pale Appearance of Rasulullaah'. A Tabraani footnote on the narrator Abyan bin Sufyaan is not tagged. Faatima is the Prophet's daughter.

summary: Tameem Daari narrates the Prophet's saying that Islaam will reach every home, bringing honour to Muslims and disgrace to the disbelievers, and says he saw this come true in his own family.
notes: The OCR spells the name 'Tarneem'; the approved entry is used.

summary: Anas narrates Umar's wish to win back six apostates from Bakr bin Waa'il by inviting them back before any execution; a second report from Abdur Rahmaan Al Qaari gives Umar's ruling on a man who reverted, and a third has Amr bin Al Aas asking how to treat a man who reverted repeatedly.
notes: Three reports are joined, followed by a footnote that Ahmad's narrators are authentic. Anas is tagged subject because he is sent on the errand and asks questions. The person sent by Abu Moosa is unnamed.

summary: Abu Imraan Jowni narrates that Umar wept on seeing a Christian monk worn out by worship, because the Qur'aan says such labour still ends in the Fire.
notes: The monk and the person who called him are unnamed.

summary: Aa'isha narrates that Abu Bakr accepted Islaam at once when the Prophet invited him, and that he then brought in several Companions over the next two days; Ibn Is'haaq and Bukhari reports are added, with an editorial correction of an error in Ibn Is'haaq.
notes: Aa'isha's report, Ibn Is'haaq's report, a Bukhari Hadith and the editor's note on Ibn Is'haaq are combined. Bukhari is a collector and is not tagged. The Companions named are tagged subject because they accept Islaam in the narration.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood narrates that the Prophet prayed that Islaam be strengthened through Umar or Abu Jahal, and Allaah answered the prayer in Umar's favour.

Thowbaan's report, promised for a later chapter, is summarised here: Umar, after leaving his sister's house, came to the Prophet, who shook him and asked what he wanted, and Umar accepted Islaam on the spot.
notes: Umar's sister Faatima is a different person from the Prophet's daughter, so she has no approved id. The text says the full Thowbaan report is quoted in a later chapter.

summary: Aslam narrates Umar's own account of how the Prophet seized his collar and called him to Islaam, and Umar testified to the Kalimah on the spot.
Amr bin Uthmaan reports Uthmaan's account of meeting the Prophet at his aunt Arwa's house; after the Prophet recited Surah Dhaariyaat on the Hereafter, Uthmaan followed him out and accepted Islaam.
notes: Amr bin Uthmaan is the narrator and Uthmaan is the source of the story, so Uthmaan is tagged subject. A Tabraani and Haythami footnote is not tagged. Amr bin Uthmaan's sahabi status is unsure.

summary: Ibn Is'haaq reports Ali's acceptance of Islaam after he found the Prophet and Khadeeja praying; Ali later recalls his father Abu Taalib's remark on seeing them pray, and Habba Urani reports seeing Ali laugh at it.
notes: Three strands are joined: Ibn Is'haaq's account, Habba Urani's report, and Ali's own remark about Abu Taalib at Nakhla. Habba Urani's sahabi status is not stated.

summary: Shaddaad bin Abdillaah reports Amr bin Abasa's account of meeting the Prophet in Makkah, accepting Islaam there, and being told to go home until the Prophet became dominant.
notes: The text says a considerable portion of this Hadith is still to be mentioned, and that part is not in this chunk. Abu Umaama is tagged subject because he asks the question that starts the report.

summary: Amr bin Abasa reports the Prophet's message of joining family ties, preserving life and roads, and worshipping one Allaah; a second account has Khaalid bin Sa'eed beaten and cast out by his father Sa'eed bin Al Aas for following the Prophet.
notes: Two reports are joined: Amr's own hadith and the Khaalid account introduced by 'according to another narration'. The text calls Sa'eed bin Al Aas 'Abu Uhayha' (his kunya), and that is tagged as the approved entry. OCR damage at 'constantly remained' and 'accompanied (RA)'.

summary: Ibn Abbaas narrates Dimaad's conversion: he came to cure the Prophet, heard the Prophet's sermon and pledged Islaam; he later refused Abu Jahal's mockery, and Ali returned camels taken from his people.
notes: Several reports are joined, with 'according to another narration' markers. The camel incident is from Abdullaah bin Abdir Rahmaan Adawi. OCR damage affects part of the Dimaad report.

summary: The Quraysh send Husayn to speak to the Prophet, who asks how many gods he worships; Husayn accepts Islaam on the Prophet's advice, and his son Imraan kisses his head, hands and feet.
notes: No narrator is named in this text. The Quraysh are unnamed.

summary: Abu Tameema Hujaymi narrates from a man of his tribe, who came to the Prophet, heard about Allaah, accepted Islaam immediately, and was then advised not to swear oaths.
notes: The man from his tribe is unnamed and is not tagged. The text itself says Abu Tameema may or may not have been present.

summary: Mu'aawiya bin Haydah narrates that he came to the Prophet, asked what Islaam is, and was told about surrender to Allaah, salaah, zakaah and the brotherhood of Muslims.
notes: This is Mu'aawiya bin Haydah, not Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan.

summary: Adi bin Haatim narrates that he first fled from the Prophet, then came to him and accepted Islaam after the Prophet addressed his objections, and was told of the coming conquest of Kisra's treasures and safe travel from Heera.
Adi bin Haatim narrates that his captured aunt was freed by the Prophet, who then spoke to Adi; Adi accepted Islaam, and the Prophet urged charity even of a date and foretold wealth and safety.
notes: The aunt is unnamed. A man with the Prophet, believed to be Ali, is not tagged because the text says 'whom they believe'. Shu'ba is a narrator within the chain.

summary: Dhul Jowshin Dhababi narrates that after Badr he refused the Prophet's invitation to Islaam, and later regretted it when he heard the Prophet had taken control of the Kabah; the Prophet had Bilaal fill his satchel with dates.
notes: Two narrations are joined ('according to another narration' gives the reason he refused). The text ends with an OCR mark '(i)'.

summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah narrates that after accepting Islaam he was renamed Basheer and placed in Ahl us-Suffa, and that he followed the Prophet to the graveyard, where the Prophet greeted the dead.
notes: OCR drops the sentence giving his original name, though 'Nadheer' appears. A footnote about Bukhari's version is mixed into the text.

summary: A man from the Baladawiyyah tribe, reporting from his grandfather, describes the Prophet, whom he saw trading, teaching leniency in buying and selling; he later accepted Islaam. Anas then narrates a separate story about inviting an uncle of the Banu Najjaar.
notes: Two reports are joined. The Baladawiyyah man and his grandfather are unnamed and are not tagged. The sentence 'stroked the head of this Sahabi' sits next to Anas's name and is ambiguous, so it is not tagged.

summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet visited a sick Jewish boy who served him, asked him to accept Islaam, and the boy did so with his father's consent.
notes: The boy and his father are unnamed.

summary: Anas narrates that the Prophet told a man to accept Islaam and he would be at peace; the man said he disliked it, and the Prophet replied, 'Even though you dislike it.'
notes: The man is unnamed.

summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr reports that on the day Makkah was conquered, the Prophet told Abu Quhaafa to accept Islaam and remain in peace.
notes: Continues on the same subject in n00039, from the same narrator.

summary: Asmaa reports that when the Prophet entered Makkah, Abu Bakr brought his father Abu Quhaafa to him; the Prophet had him sit before him, he accepted Islaam, and the Prophet advised him on his white hair.

Mughiera bin Shu'ba narrates that the Prophet invited Abu Jahal to Islaam in a Makkah alley, and Abu Jahal refused, saying that the Bani Qusay had taken each office in turn and he would never accept a Nabi from among them.
notes: Trailing OCR debris '(,)' is ignored.
